Runs on the Winlator runtime (LGPL-2.1), which bundles Wine and Box64. Mod Hub interaction patterns reference StS2 Launcher Mod Manager (MIT). Full notices ship in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.

Lets box64 skip checks it normally makes while turning the game’s x86 code into ARM. It can crash or corrupt the picture on some scenes; turn it back off if anything looks wrong. Applies on the next launch.

The game has no frame limit, so it renders as fast as the cores let it and spends the battery doing it. Holding it off the fastest cores costs speed and buys back running time. Applies on the next launch.

The game is kept inside the app, where it loads quickly. Mods go in DD1/mods, and replacement files and DLLs in DD1/overrides; both are brought in when you press Play. A game still in phone storage (DD1/game) is moved inside, which copies about 4 GB and needs that much free space for a while.
The game is copied to %1$s and then removed from where it was. This takes several minutes. Saves are not affected.

Without storage access the game is downloaded inside the app. Mods in DD1/mods and files in DD1/overrides cannot be read until access is granted.
The game is inside the app

File managers cannot reach the app\'s own storage. Files put in DD1/overrides are laid over the game each time you press Play, in the same folders: DD1/overrides/_windows/win64/example.dll lands beside Darkest.exe. Take a file out and the game\'s own comes back. Mods go in DD1/mods.
Moving the game into the app. This happens once, and loading is much faster afterwards.
Not enough free space to move the game inside the app. It needs about %1$.1f GB free; free some space and tap the notice on the home screen to try again.
The game is in phone storage (DD1/game), where loading can take minutes. Tap here to move it into the app.
Move the game into the app?

In phone storage every scene change reads thousands of files through Android\'s storage layer and can take many minutes. Inside the app it takes seconds. Moving copies about 4 GB, then removes the old copy, which also takes a few minutes. Saves are not affected. Mods move to DD1/mods, and files that replace game files go in DD1/overrides.
DD1/overrides is in phone storage, so this needs storage access.
Game moved. Removing the old copy (%1$d files so far). Keep the app open until this finishes.

Draws with the Qualcomm driver the device ships instead of Turnip. Try it on the newest Snapdragon parts where Turnip stutters badly, such as the Galaxy S26 Ultra (Adreno 840). Tried on few devices so far.

Used only when the graphics driver chosen above includes Vortek. Loads an AdrenoTools driver file you downloaded (a zip, such as a Turnip build for Adreno 8xx) in place of the device driver. The launcher ships no driver, so only use a file from a source you trust. If the game draws nothing, go back to the device driver. Takes effect the next time you press Play.

Puts frames per second and GPU, CPU and memory use over the game. With these numbers beside a report of stutter, the cause is much easier to find. Takes effect the next time you press Play.

While the game runs, what Wine and box64 print goes to DD1/logs/wine-log.txt and a description of the device and settings to DD1/logs/device.txt, and what the app and the graphics driver log to DD1/logs/logcat.txt. Attach both to a bug report - they are often the only way to see what went wrong on a device we do not have. The run before is kept under the same names with -previous. It can slow the game a little, so leave it off unless you need it. Takes effect the next time you press Play.
Takes effect the next time you press Play. If a change makes things worse, come back and set Automatic.
You are running %s. The new APK is on the release page; download it there and install over this one - the game, the saves and the mods stay where they are.
Let the runtime menu open during the game

Off by default. It is the panel that slides in from the left, and a controller opens it by accident: a button the game does not use arrives as Back, and the runtime answers Back by opening the menu. Turn it on if you want the runtime\'s own keyboard, task manager or exit. Takes effect the next time you press Play.
